newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Xerox Q3 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Xerox Q3 earnings.

text.p: Xerox Corp on Friday reported third quarter earnings of $0.68 per share. The First Call estimate for the quarter was $0.82 per share.
Following is the full text of the press release.

STAMFORD, Conn., Oct. 18 /PRNewswire/ -- Income from Xerox Corporation's document processing business declined 2 percent in the third quarter to $250 million, compared with $256 million in the third quarter of 1995. Revenues grew 4 percent in the quarter to $4.2 billion, compared with $4.0 billion last year.

Document processing primary earnings per share were 71 cents in the quarter, compared with 74 cents in the third quarter of 1995. Fully diluted earnings per share were 68 cents, compared with 70 cents a year ago.

"I am disappointed in the results this quarter," said Xerox Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul A. Allaire. "Although enterprise printing revenue growth accelerated in all major geographic areas, overall revenue growth was adversely affected by a modest decline in black-and-white copier revenues. Our investments in sales coverage and promotion did not yield the results we expected in the quarter."

Total revenues on a pre-currency basis grew 5 percent, with end-user equipment sales growing 6 percent. Digital enterprise printing revenues grew 23 percent and black-and-white copier revenues declined 4 percent. Enterprise printing revenues are now 30 percent of total revenues and black-and-white copier revenues are 56 percent of total revenues.

Black-and-white copier revenues declined as a result of several factors, including price pressure and difficult economic environments in Europe and a number of emerging markets. A significant slowdown in growth in Brazil followed two years of exceptional growth.
Total document processing revenues in the United States grew 5 percent in the quarter, while Rank Xerox revenues increased 2 percent and revenues in other operations grew 6 percent.

As a result of hiring in the company's fast-growing document outsourcing business, worldwide employment increased during the quarter by 400 to 87,000. Hiring in sales and manufacturing was offset by reductions in other areas.

Gross profit grew 4 percent but research and development expenses increased 8 percent, and selling, administrative and general expenses grew 10 percent, somewhat faster than anticipated, primarily as a result of additional investments in sales coverage and promotion, new product advertising and marketing support.

"We expect some improvement in the fourth quarter, with somewhat slower growth in costs and expenses," Xerox Chairman Allaire said. "We continue to be optimistic about 1997. The entire management team is focused on growth and productivity. We've made investments in our sales force and new products which will increase our competitiveness in the market. Overall, our strategic direction remains sound; our technology is second to none; and the market opportunities remain significant.

"Our product development is focused on the fastest growing segments of the $100 billion global document processing market: production publishing, color copying and printing, electronic printing and office network systems. For example, our DocuColor 40, a 40 page-a-minute full-color document production system introduced in April, has exceeded our expectations. And 1997 will be an even more important year for product introductions as we expand our digital product capabilities."

In the first nine months of the year, document processing income was $780 million, compared with $697 million in the first three quarters of 1995. Revenues were $12.3 billion in the first nine months compared with $11.8 billion a year ago. Primary earnings per share for the first nine months were $2.24, compared with $2.01, and fully diluted earnings per share were $2.14, compared with $1.91 in the first nine months of 1995.

Total company income in the third quarter was $250 million, compared with $236 million a year ago, including a $20 million loss from discontinued operations. Primary earnings per share were 71 cents, compared with 68 cents a year ago, and fully diluted earnings per share were 68 cents, compared with 65 cents. The company's insurance and other financial services businesses are reported as discontinued operations.

Total company income was $780 million in the first nine months of the year, compared with $621 million last year, including a $76 million loss from discontinued operations. Primary earnings per share were $2.24, compared with $1.78 a year ago, and fully diluted earnings per share were $2.14, compared with $1.70.

In September, Xerox reported that agreements to sell the Talegen Holdings, Inc., and The Resolution Group, Inc., insurance units had been terminated. The units are now being marketed separately. The company expects its strategy of exiting the financial services business to be substantially completed by the end of 1997.
On Feb. 5, the board of directors authorized the repurchase of up to $1 billion of Xerox common stock. By Sept. 30, the company had repurchased 5 million shares for $232 million.

Total common shares used to calculate primary earnings per share in the quarter were 333.6 million, compared with 332.4 million in the corresponding 1995 period, and 333.6 million in the first nine months, compared with 330.4 million last year. Total common shares used to calculate fully diluted earnings per share in the quarter were 364.3 million, compared with 364.5 million in the corresponding 1995 period, and 364.3 million in the first nine months, compared with 362.5 million last year.
